subject.title: fix(gateway): cap pricing cache entries to prevent unbounded memory growth (#101543)

question: Should maintainers use this 1000-entry timestamp-LRU PR as the canonical cache-cap fix after it stops retaining rows absent from successful refreshes, or consolidate around another open candidate such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102242?
rationale: Multiple open PRs fix the same gateway pricing-cache memory issue with different cap sizes and retention policies, and that choice can affect cost-estimate availability after upgrade.

options.title: Fix This PR Then Reconsider
options.body: Keep this branch viable only after it ranks entries from the current refresh payload rather than carrying absent cached rows forward.

options.title: Prefer The 4096-Entry Candidate
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102242 if maintainers prefer its map-order, refreshed-row-only approach and larger cap.

options.title: Ask For Consolidation
options.body: Pause the candidate branches until contributors converge on one cap size, eviction policy, proof set, and test shape.

recommendation.title: Fix This PR Then Reconsider
recommendation.body: Keep this branch viable only after it ranks entries from the current refresh payload rather than carrying absent cached rows forward.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history in the gateway pricing-cache and nearby memory-bound pricing fetch paths.
